script.analysis: All 15,355 stored characters read in one contiguous range with canonical hash match. Hook: Target-parking-lot overdraft math vs coworker Sarah's Cabo trips, "one boring decision" now $43K; subscribe CTA. Jessica (Civic, $500/month since 22) vs Amanda (BMW, car payments) at 28/35/45/55/65 ($4.32M vs $461K). Finding $500 (subscriptions $273, dining $280 and their 30-year values), $500/month 40-year math and contribution share, 10/20/30-year milestones, 10-and-stop vs 30-years comparison, S&P history and rolling periods, crash recoveries, JPMorgan best-days study, 46% no retirement savings and $88K median 55-64, present bias/loss aversion/lifestyle inflation, industry incentives, Ronald Read, Sylvia Bloom, Grace Groner, Fidelity 401k millionaires, retiree reality, fees with named index funds, $748 car payment value, Roth IRA and 401k mechanics with 2026 figures, five steps, cost-of-waiting, two-futures close. Dense, concrete and motivating, with many correct figures and several numeric slips; no community CTA. ASR errors ("R Sera", "$29,78", "$1,50", "VO") preserved; not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:15355 $500/month at 10% (monthly): 40 years ~$3.16M with $240K contributed (92.4% growth), 20 years ~$379K, 30 years ~$1.13M - correct; "after 10 years about $12,000" is wrong (~$102K; likely garbled ASR or misstatement). $1M to $2M ~6.7 years correct. Jessica at 35/45/55/65 (~$159K/$533K/$1.54M/$4.28M) close to stated figures. $280 and $273 per month for 30 years at 10% (~$633K/~$617K) correct. $5,000/year 25-35 then stop vs 35-65 at 8% with beginning-of-year deposits: ~$787K vs ~$612K, difference ~$175K - correct.

0:15355 S&P ~10% nominal since 1926, ~-86% Depression decline, no negative 20-year nominal total-return period, COVID recovery ~5 months and 2008 ~5.5 years consistent with standard histories; "worst 30-year return 4.3%" unverified. JPMorgan 2003-2022 $10,000: $64,844 fully invested vs ~$29,708 missing 10 best days, with 7 of the 10 best days in bear markets - consistent with JPMorgan Guide to Retirement. 46% of households without retirement accounts consistent with SCF 2022; loss aversion ~2.25 (Tversky & Kahneman 1992) correct.

0:15355 Ronald Read (died 2014 at 92, ~$8M estate, $4.8M hospital, $1.2M library), Sylvia Bloom (~$9M, $6.24M to charity) and Grace Groner (three Abbott shares in 1935 for $180, ~$7.2M at death in 2010) consistent with widely reported accounts; "bought dividend stocks every week for 70 years" embellishes. Fidelity ~595,000 401k millionaires consistent with 2025 reports; 14.1%/26-year averages unverified. Social Security average $1,976 is the 2025 figure; 2026 average is ~$2,071 after the 2.8% COLA (video published Feb 2026). "The average doctor dies with $1.2 million in debt" has no support and is implausible as an average.

0:15355 Fees: $500/month 30 years at ~9.97% vs 9% gives ~$1.123M vs ~$915K, a ~$208K difference - the stored "$29,000 difference" contradicts the following "quarter million" (likely garbled). FXAIX 0.015%, VOO 0.03%, SWPPX 0.02% expense ratios correct. $748 x 30 years at 10% ~$1.69M correct; $100/month 30 years ~$226K correct, but $3.33/day (~$101/month) gives ~$229K, not $250K. 2026 Roth IRA $7,500 ($625/month) and phase-out starts $153K single / $242K MFJ correct; $500 pre-tax contribution in 22% bracket reduces take-home ~$390 (federal only); 50% match on 6% of $60K = $150/month correct. Cost of waiting understated: to reach $3.16M with 39/35/30 years at 10% requires ~$553/~$833/~$1,399 monthly, not $520/$690/$1,050.
